channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: UK Suspends Thames Water Administration Plan, The Times Reports
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has halted plans to place Thames Water into administration because of concerns about the cost and legal risk, The Times reported, citing unidentified officials.
item.dc:creator: Rob Verdonck

item.title: Trump Laments Lack of US Aluminum Amid Trade Row With Canada
item.description: President Donald Trump, who has argued that the US does not need Canada, lamented Monday that his northern neighbor did have something he wants: aluminum.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Josh Wingrove

item.title: Venezuela to End Checkpoints Long Used to Police Dissent
item.description: Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez said she will eliminate police checkpoints in cities, dismantling one of the key tools widely used for surveillance and repression under Chavismo over the past decade.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Laya and Andreina Itriago

item.title: S. Korea Denies Report US Proposed It Buy Stake in Westinghouse
item.description: South Korea’s government denied a report that the US had proposed Seoul acquire a stake in Westinghouse Electric Co., pushing back on suggestions that the American nuclear company could become part of the countries’ strategic investment program.
item.dc:creator: Seyoon Kim

item.title: South Korea Vows to Turn Trump Overtures into North Korea Talks
item.description: South Korea and the US agreed to maintain close coordination on efforts to revive dialogue with North Korea, days after Pyongyang rebuffed President Donald Trump’s overtures and launched a barrage of short-range ballistic missiles.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Canada to Unveil Trump Tariff Response Including Loans, Benefits
item.description: Canada’s government on Tuesday will announce a range of measures to “protect and support” its workers and businesses in response to 50% US tariffs which were applied to about $20 billion of its annual exports on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Thomas Seal

item.title: Bessent’s Iran D-Day Threat Hinges on Willingness to Hit China
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s threat to unleash an “economic D-Day” against Iran risks setting the US on a collision course with China, its main trading partner.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle and Yash Roy

item.title: Putin Intends to Meet With Modi at Forum in Kyrgyzstan Next Week
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he aims to meet with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a regional forum next week, while calling for stepped-up trade cooperation between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey

item.title: Bessent Unleashes ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ on Iran | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/24/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA) says he will not vote “for a single dollar” to fund what he calls a failed and illegal war, arguing Congress must prevent it from becoming a “forever war.” Stephen Moore, former Trump economic advisor, says China is key to the success of the Trump administration's secondary sanctions targeting countries that continue to do business with Iran. Rob Bonta, Attorney General of California, says he canceled a meeting with Paramount over its proposed merger with Warner Bros., accusing the company of “playing games” and leaking details of confidential negotiations to the press. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ‘Flunky,’ ‘Loser’: Trump Trades Wild Insults With Canada’s Ford
item.description: The trade war between the US and Canada erupted into an extraordinary exchange of insults and threats between President Donald Trump and Doug Ford, the leader of Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal

item.title: Burnham Plans US Trip Next Month to Lobby Trump on Ukraine Needs
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he and other European leaders plan to travel to the US next month to lobby President Donald Trump to let Ukraine access some of its Patriot air defense missile stocks ahead of the winter.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Lutnick’s Intervention in Canada Talks Draws Praise, Blame
item.description: US-Canada trade talks collapsed after last-minute pressure from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, according to people familiar with the matter, leaving President Donald Trump to impose new tariffs and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing retaliation.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Alicia Diaz and Catherine Lucey

item.title: Moore: China Key to Success of Iran Sanctions
item.description: Stephen Moore, former Trump economic advisor, says China is key to the success of the Trump administration's secondary sanctions targeting countries that continue to do business with Iran. Moore also says he is “not a fan” of the escalating tariffs between the US and Canada, warning that higher input prices could make things more expensive at home. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Donors Aren’t Translating to Big Success in US Midterms
item.description: This US midterm election season is on track to be the most expensive on record. Federal PACs have already brought in $4.7 billion. But in some races, big spending is backfiring.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Holder and Rachael Lewis-Krisky

item.title: Rep. Auchincloss: Won’t Fund ‘Illegal’ War
item.description: Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA) says he will not vote “for a single dollar” to fund what he calls a failed and illegal war, arguing Congress must prevent it from becoming a “forever war.” Auchincloss says the Trump administration’s actions show it is trying to find an exit from a war it has lost, despite its rhetoric about an “economic D-Day” against Iran. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Warns of Economic Asphyxiation | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/24/2026
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered remarks to kick off the week, announcing a plan to to sever Iran from the global economy and threatening all nations to cut ties with Iran. A panel of Bloomberg experts -- Chief US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey, Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee, and Senior National Political Correspondent Nancy Cook -- react to Bessent's remarks, including the plan for bond buybacks next month. Then, TerraPower CEO Chris Levesque, discusses his company's plan to build a second nuclear power plant in the US this year. Plus, Bloomberg News Toronto Bureau Chief Melissa Shin breaks down President Trump's latest tariff actions on Canada and threats to escalate the trade fight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California AG Bonta on Mail Ballots, Paramount Talks and Meta Trial
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta discusses why he canceled talks with Paramount over the company’s merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Speaking on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition," Bonta also comments on the US Supreme Court siding with President Donald Trump over his plan to use the Postal Service to impose new restrictions on the distribution of mail ballots and Meta Platforms being sued by a bipartisan coalition of states on allegations of deceiving the public. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Sides With Trump for Now on Mail Ballots
item.description: The US Supreme Court sided with President Donald Trump over his plan to use the Postal Service to impose new restrictions on the distribution of mail ballots. Kate Sullivan reports on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Sides With Trump for Now on Mail Ballot Curbs
item.description: The US Supreme Court gave President Donald Trump a temporary victory on his push to use the Postal Service to limit the distribution of mail ballots in the November midterms, while leaving open the prospect of a renewed challenge in the coming days.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: US Eyes China Overcapacity Tariffs of 7.5% Before Xi Visits
item.description: The US is set to impose a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods over allegations of excess manufacturing capacity before a planned summit between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump next month, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Lucille Liu and Jenny Leonard
